note: Hand-authored `.SYNTHETIC.`-caveated fixtures for `OpenAiProvider` (flow 183, T6 / AC1, AC5). NO live `OPENAI_API_KEY` was available in this environment (see this flow's description.md 'Known, explicit deviation from the docpack' and acceptance-criteria.md AC1). Every fixture here was built from CURRENT vendor documentation researched live via WebSearch/WebFetch during this task (2026-08-20/21) against https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/responses/methods/create, https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/responses/streaming-events, https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/responses/methods/retrieve, and multiple corroborating community/SDK-issue-tracker threads for the two details the official reference pages did not fully spell out (the terminal `error` event's actual field nesting, and the reasoning-summary streaming event name) — NOT captured from a real API call, and NOT training-data recall. `captured: false` on every entry below, by construction (no key available), mirroring the honest-gap pattern `keryx-mcp-client`'s manifest used for its unreproducible fixtures and the sibling `fixtures/provider-breadth/gemini/manifest.json`.

provenance.method: Hand-authored from live-researched current OpenAI Responses API (POST /v1/responses, stream:true) REST documentation. Every wire-shape decision below cites the specific research finding that grounds it, not an assumption.
provenance.inputItemShapeConfirmed: The `input` array item shape for a plain message is {"type":"message","role":"user"|"assistant","content":[{"type":"input_text"|"output_text","text":...}]} — confirmed via the official API reference (developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/responses/methods/create) and independently corroborated by a WebSearch across multiple sources describing the same {type:'message', role, content:[{type:'input_text', text}]} shape. Tool-loop items are SIBLING items in the flat `input` array (not content blocks nested inside one message, unlike Anthropic): {"type":"function_call","call_id","name","arguments"} for the assistant's own call, {"type":"function_call_output","call_id","output"} for the tool's result — both confirmed verbatim from the same official reference page.
provenance.instructionsFieldConfirmed: `instructions` is a top-level sibling of `input`, not folded into the input array — confirmed by the official reference; this adapter maps `NormalizedRequest.systemInstruction` there directly.
provenance.toolCallCorrelationKeyConfirmed: `call_id` (NOT the item's own `id`) is the correlation key threaded through `response.output_item.added`'s `item.call_id`, `response.function_call_arguments.delta/.done`'s implicit correlation (via `item_id`, which this adapter resolves back to the pending call's `call_id`), and the request-side `function_call`/`function_call_output` items — confirmed via WebSearch (GitHub issue discussion of llama.cpp's /v1/responses SSE implementation explicitly naming 'both call_id and id fields are required by the API SDK schemas', consistent with the flow's own dispatch instructions).
provenance.streamingEventCatalogConfirmed: The event `type` strings response.created, response.output_item.added/.done, response.output_text.delta/.done, response.function_call_arguments.delta/.done, response.completed were confirmed via the official streaming-events reference page's TypeScript event-union listing and the output_item reference subpage. response.failed/.incomplete were confirmed via this flow's plan.md research (not independently re-confirmed live in this task, carried forward as researched).
provenance.errorEventShapeDiscrepancyFound: A genuine documentation-vs-reality discrepancy was found and is handled defensively rather than trusted either way: the official reference for the terminal `error` streaming event nominally documents `code`/`message`/`param` as fields FLAT on the event object, but a first-hand OpenAI Developer Community bug report (openai community thread 'Responses, Bug: error event shape is wrong between documentation and SDKs and reality') quotes an ACTUAL observed payload with those same fields NESTED under an `error` key: {"type":"error","sequence_number":N,"error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","code":null,"message":"...","param":null}}. This adapter's extractErrorFields() checks the nested `error.{code,message,param}` shape FIRST, falling back to flat fields, so it tolerates either documented-vs-real variant rather than committing to one.
provenance.emptyMessageBugConfirmed: The documented (third-party-reported) bug that a context-length overflow on the Responses API STREAMING path returns a terminal error event with an EMPTY error.message was independently corroborated via a GitHub issue search (maximhq/bifrost#4413, filed against a proxy that surfaces the same upstream OpenAI behavior) quoting the exact empty `{"error":{"message":""}}` shape and confirming the same request returns a proper `code:"context_length_exceeded"` on the NON-streaming Responses path and on Chat Completions streaming — i.e. the detail exists upstream, it is specifically THIS streaming path that drops it. This adapter substitutes a generic, non-empty, honestly-hedged message rather than ever surfacing an empty string to the operator.
provenance.reasoningSummaryEventConfirmed: `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta` (fields: type, item_id, output_index, summary_index, delta, sequence_number) is the confirmed reasoning-summary streaming event, corroborated independently by (a) the official streaming-events reference's event-union listing, (b) an openai-python SDK issue (#2311) discussing this exact event type's Python binding, and (c) an OpenAI Developer Community thread discussing it alongside a related `response.reasoning_summary.delta` event. This REFINES plan.md's flagged uncertainty (which called the exact event shape 'unconfirmed, verify before claiming true') into a confirmed `reasoningMetadata: true` claim, backed by 3 independent corroborating sources rather than one.
provenance.visionShapeConfirmedButNotWired: The `input_image` content-part shape ({"type":"input_image","detail":"low"|"high"|"auto"|"original","image_url":<string, optional>,"file_id":<string, optional>}) WAS confirmed via the official API reference during this task's research — but this adapter's toResponsesInput() only builds text content parts; request-side image serialization is not implemented. Per plan.md's 'unconfirmed-or-unwired -> false' rule, `vision` stays `false` despite the shape being confirmed, because the capability itself is not exercised end-to-end.
provenance.contextLengthExceededCodeConfirmed: `context_length_exceeded` is the confirmed `code` string on the standard `{error:{message,type,param,code}}` HTTP error body for a 400 on the non-streaming path, corroborated by the same maximhq/bifrost#4413 issue and by multiple independent OpenAI Developer Community / troubleshooting-guide threads describing the identical code string for this exact condition.

text-stream.SYNTHETIC.sse.case: Clean streamed text response: response.created, response.output_item.added (message item), two response.output_text.delta chunks, response.output_text.done, response.output_item.done, response.completed carrying usage.{input_tokens,output_tokens,total_tokens,output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens}.
text-stream.SYNTHETIC.sse.caveat: Hand-authored from the researched wire shape above. Field values (ids, token counts, text content) are illustrative fixture data, not observed from a real call.

tool-call-stream.SYNTHETIC.sse.case: Tool-call round trip: response.output_item.added for a function_call item (carrying both item.id and item.call_id, distinct values — proving the adapter correlates on call_id, not id), two response.function_call_arguments.delta fragments, response.function_call_arguments.done with the full concatenated arguments JSON, response.output_item.done, response.completed.
tool-call-stream.SYNTHETIC.sse.caveat: Hand-authored from the researched wire shape above. The distinct id/call_id values are deliberately different strings in this fixture specifically to make a correlation-key bug (accidentally keying on `id`) produce a visibly wrong `toolCallId` in a test assertion, rather than silently passing by coincidence.

error-context-overflow.SYNTHETIC.sse.case: The documented empty-message context-overflow bug: a terminal `error` event with `error.code:"context_length_exceeded"` and `error.message:""` (empty string), exactly matching the maximhq/bifrost#4413-reported shape.
error-context-overflow.SYNTHETIC.sse.caveat: Hand-authored from the researched/corroborated bug shape above. Exercises the adapter's defensive empty-message substitution — the adapter's yielded NormalizedError.message must never be empty even though the upstream fixture's message field is.

inline (in openai-provider.test.ts).case: 401 authentication, 429 rate_limit (with Retry-After), 400 invalid_request / context_overflow, 5xx unavailable HTTP-level error bodies; credential-redaction assertions.
inline (in openai-provider.test.ts).caveat: Built inline in the test file (not separate fixture files) for locality with the assertions they support. Same provenance as the file-based fixtures: hand-authored from the researched wire shapes documented above, not captured.

gaps: AC1 is explicitly NOT MET by this flow (see acceptance-criteria.md): no live OPENAI_API_KEY was available to verify these fixtures against a real POST /v1/responses call. Live verification remains an open follow-up.

response.failed and response.incomplete event shapes are carried forward from plan.md's prior research and were not independently re-confirmed live in this task (no fixture exercises them separately from the response.completed / terminal error paths that ARE fixtured) — the adapter's handling of both is implemented per plan.md's summary, but is the least-independently-corroborated part of this adapter.

The genuine documentation-vs-reality discrepancy on the terminal `error` event's field nesting (flat per the official reference vs. nested per a first-hand community bug report) was not resolved by finding a single authoritative current shape — it was resolved defensively (accept either) rather than by picking one, which is itself an honest gap: a live call would show which shape (or whether both exist depending on error subtype) is actually current.
vision (input_image) is documented/confirmed at the shape level but NOT wired end-to-end (see provenance.visionShapeConfirmedButNotWired above) — capability stays false, not a guess.

reasoning_delta's exact interaction with parallel tool calls (does a reasoning summary interleave with multiple concurrent function_call items, or always precede them) was not specifically researched — this adapter treats reasoning_summary_text.delta as an independent event stream keyed by its own item_id/summary_index, not correlated to any specific tool call, which is the conservative reading of the confirmed event shape.
tokenCounting stays false: no dedicated OpenAI token-counting endpoint analogous to Gemini's {model}:countTokens was found in this task's research, and none is wired.
